chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Mutawakkinn (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, who said: Abu Nu'aym al-Balghi narrated to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dharr, from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (may the mercy of Allah be upon him), who said:

I was holding the hand of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while we were walking together, and we continued looking at the sun until it set. I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, where does it set?' He said: 'In the sky, then it is raised from one sky to another until it is raised to the highest seventh sky, until it is beneath the Throne. It prostrates, and the angels entrusted with it prostrate with it.'
Then it says: 'O my Lord, from where do You command me to rise? From my setting place or from my rising place?'
And the sun runs [on its course] toward its stopping point. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.

He means thereby the making of the Mighty Lord in His dominion, the Knowing of His creation. He said: Then Gabriel comes to it with a garment of light from the light of the Throne, according to the measures of the hours of the day, lengthening them in summer or shortening them in winter, or something in between in autumn and spring.
He said: It wears that garment as one of you wears his clothes, then it goes with it in the atmosphere of the sky until it rises from its rising place.
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'It is as if I see it being held back for the duration of three nights, then it is not clothed with light and is commanded to rise from its west.'
When the sun is wrapped up [in darkness] * And when the stars fall, dispersing,

And the moon is similar in its rising place and its course in the horizon of the sky and its setting and its rising to the seventh sky, and it prostrates beneath the Throne. Then Gabriel comes to it with the garment from the light of the Throne.
He made the sun a shining light and the moon a visible light
Abu Dharr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Then I withdrew with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and we prayed the Maghrib prayer.
ai.seo_question: Where does the sun go after it sets according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Tawhid highlights the Shia understanding of the sun's physical movement and prostration beneath the Throne, linking it to the verse 'And the sun runs to its resting place' (36:38) as a description of its daily journey rather than just its orbit. The text elaborates on the cosmic mechanism where Gabriel clothes the sun in light from the Throne to regulate day length, illustrating Allah's precise control over celestial bodies. This cosmological view reinforces the concept of Tawhid by demonstrating how natural phenomena are directly governed by divine command and angelic execution.
